clue.text: The trawlerman's haul after deducting expenses?

definitions.text: The trawlerman's haul after deducting expenses?

parts.words: The trawlerman's haul after deducting expenses
parts.note: a fishing boat's catch comes in a mesh, and the gain left once costs are taken off has a matching business name

explanation.surface: A fisherman totting up what his catch is really worth after costs.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure left after expenses is the earnings in accounting terms, and a trawler's catch literally sits in its mesh.

clue.text: Quixotic Engineers reverting to bombast

indicators.note: reverting means turning back, so the letters for engineers are read backwards

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
bombast is ranting, inflated talk

explanation.surface: Military engineers lapsing into pompous speech like Don Quixote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverting' turns RE (Royal Engineers) into ER, then RANT follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Quixote was a knight errant, so wandering in search of adventure is quixotic.

clue.text: A clerk who sends off a bill?

explanation.surface: An office worker posting out invoices.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mails letters is literally one who posts; a bill stuck on a wall is a placard.

clue.text: Gross distortion about eastern female of frightful proportions

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the letter for eastern
a distortion twists the shape, so the letters of the word gross are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something grossly distorted about a woman from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distortion' rearranges GROSS to OGRSS, and 'about' puts it round E.
explanation.definitionFit: A she-monster of fairy tales is huge and terrifying, a giantess who eats people.

clue.text: Helping to crew an assemblage where it shouldn't be?

indicators.note: an assemblage is a putting-together, so the letters of the preceding words are reassembled

explanation.surface: Lending a hand to staff some gathering, oddly misplaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assemblage' rearranges the fifteen letters of HELPING TO CREW AN; 'helping to crew' looks like a sailing phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misplaced is out of its proper position, located wrongly.

clue.text: Woe betide the man he catches stealing an art masterpiece

definitions.text: Woe betide the man he catches stealing

explanation.surface: A policeman nabbing a thief who has lifted a famous painting.
explanation.walkthrough: John Constable was an English landscape painter, so one of his canvases is 'a Constable'.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer arrests thieves; a painting by John Constable is a celebrated artwork.

clue.text: Chinese detective drowned in English river cutting

indicators.note: drowned in means submerged within, so the detective goes inside the river

parts.note: the Trent is a major river of the English Midlands
Charlie Chan is the fictional Chinese-American detective of novels and films

explanation.surface: A Chinese sleuth found dead in an English river channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' looks like a noun (a channel dug beside the river) but is the adjective meaning incisive.
explanation.definitionFit: Incisive, biting remarks are sharp and penetrating.

clue.text: Female predator that flies over a ship at the mouth of the Medway

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the first pieces sit above the next

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
an erne is a sea eagle, a bird of prey
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A female bird of prey swooping over a vessel at a river estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheerness is a port town in Kent, at the estuary of the River Medway in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent town of this name stands on the estuary where the Medway river enters the Thames.

clue.text: A fraction too slow to get a place usually

definitions.text: too slow to get a place usually

explanation.surface: A runner finishing just a fraction too slow for a placing.
explanation.walkthrough: In horse-race betting a 'place' usually pays on the first three finishers.
explanation.definitionFit: One part in four is a quarter; finishing just behind the top three misses a placed bet.

clue.text: Flat out in favour of new treats?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters of treats

explanation.surface: Exhausted, someone supports a fresh batch of goodies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges TREATS to STRATE after PRO. 'Flat out' suggests full speed, but here means lying face down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying stretched face down on the ground is lying prone, utterly flat.

clue.text: Can sue for time to pay a foreign bill

definitions.text: time to pay a foreign bill

indicators.note: for here means in exchange for, so the letters of can sue are traded for a new order

explanation.surface: Suing someone to gain time to pay an overseas invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is the anagram signal on CAN SUE. The answer is an old banking term.
explanation.definitionFit: In banking, the customary period allowed before a bill of exchange drawn abroad falls due.

clue.text: Freely living a dog's life?

parts.note: a dog free of its lead is roaming at liberty, and a person let loose acts the same way

explanation.surface: Living without restraint like a carefree hound.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog freed from its lead runs loose; figuratively, released without restraint.

clue.text: Route followed by an Afghan tribesman

indicators.note: followed by places the second piece after the first

parts.note: a path is a route
taken as written

explanation.surface: A road taken by a tribesman from Afghanistan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pashtun people of Afghanistan and Pakistan were called this in British India.

clue.text: Most inexpensive type of ring

parts.note: ring suggests jewellery, but here means a telephone call, the cheapest being within the same area

explanation.surface: Shopping for the cheapest engagement band.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone call within one's own area was the cheapest tariff.

clue.text: By far the best of the aston no my students?

definitions.text: By far the best of the aston no my students?

parts.words: By far the best of the aston no my students
parts.note: the top learner in a class is its brightest, and one studying the heavens fittingly shines like a celestial body

explanation.surface: The top learner in an astronomy class.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'aston no my' is a misprint for 'astronomy'; the top learner among those who study the heavens is fittingly a celestial body.
explanation.definitionFit: The best learner in a class is its brightest, and astronomy studies the bodies that shine at night.

clue.text: Deals exclusively with evidence that spring has arrived?

explanation.surface: Someone handles only proof that spring is here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. The first sense is a verb, omits; the second is foliage appearing on trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Excluding something means omitting it; foliage appearing on trees in springtime is the second sense.

clue.text: Are set back a number of years

indicators.note: set back means placed in reverse, so the letters of are are read backwards

explanation.surface: Being delayed costs several years.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long period of time spanning many years.

clue.text: Some of the people Rebecca stood before

indicators.note: some of means only a portion of the words that follow supply the letters

explanation.surface: Rebecca stood in front of part of the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some of' picks letters across 'peoplE REbecca'; 'the' and 'stood' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic word is a poetic preposition meaning prior to.

clue.text: A literary connection

parts.note: a connection in writing is a conjunction, the commonest little joining word

explanation.surface: A link between two authors.
explanation.definitionFit: The commonest conjunction joins words and clauses in written language.

clue.text: Running the railways thus would be asking for trouble!

definitions.text: Running the railways thus would be asking for trouble!

parts.words: Running the railways thus would be asking for trouble
parts.note: trains sent along the incorrect tracks would crash, and the idiom means acting in a mistaken way

explanation.surface: A remark about the dangers of mismanaging a rail network.
explanation.definitionFit: Trains on incorrect tracks literally court disaster; the idiom means pursuing a mistaken approach.

clue.text: Close finish

explanation.surface: A close finish to a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean conclusion: the close of a day, the finish of a story.

clue.text: A turbulent river reach

indicators.note: turbulent means churned up, so the letters of river are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A rough river stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turbulent' rearranges RIVER to RRIVE after A. 'reach' looks like a noun for a stretch of river but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To get to a destination is to come to it.

clue.text: Chirpy creature, not a gentleman in the American secret service

indicators.note: in means the second piece sits inside the first

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably, no gentleman

explanation.surface: A cheerful creature, a bounder working for American intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chirpy' suggests cheerful, but the insect literally chirps.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect is known for its loud, shrill song in summer.

clue.text: A fish in charge of a fungus?

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish put in command of a mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Gill-bearing mushrooms, such as the field mushroom and the fly amanita, belong to this group.

clue.text: River detectives brought in to settle the matter

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside, so the detectives go inside the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
CID is the British police Criminal Investigation Department

explanation.surface: Detectives called to a river to resolve a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To resolve an issue or make up one's mind is to determine it.

clue.text: A fount of small type

parts.note: fount suggests printing type, but here it is a water source, and a small one is a little spring

explanation.surface: A printer's set of tiny letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fount' is also the British spelling of font, a set of printing type, which is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A little spring, a tiny source of water rising from the ground.

clue.text: Old oil vessel in which I go for a sail

indicators.note: in which means the following piece is placed inside the vessel

parts.note: a cruse is an old word for a small earthenware jar for oil

explanation.surface: Sailing in an old oil tanker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old oil vessel' suggests a tanker ship, but a cruse is a small biblical jar.
explanation.definitionFit: To travel by boat for pleasure is to voyage leisurely at sea.

clue.text: Told Maria the clumsy version

indicators.note: a version is a different rendering, so the letters of told maria are given another arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone told Maria the awkward account of events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' rearranges the letters of TOLD MARIA; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept, awkward and bungling in movement or handling.

clue.text: In store? Well, no

explanation.surface: Is it in stock? Er, no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well, no' means not well, that is ill in bed; the first sense is put away for later.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods stored away are kept in reserve; a person confined to bed by illness is the second sense.

clue.text: Graduate of University College Hospital caught in the act and corrupted

indicators.note: caught in means trapped inside, so the pieces go inside the act

parts.note: a deed is an act
BA is a Bachelor of Arts
UC is short for University College

explanation.surface: A hospital graduate caught red-handed, morally depraved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught in the act' looks like the idiom, but 'caught in' puts BAUCH inside DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Debased and depraved, led into immoral excess.
